name: Midline longitudinal approach (periprosthetic knee)
corridor: Reused full-thickness midline TKA incision with a medial parapatellar arthrotomy, extensible to the quadriceps or tibial tubercle, used for periprosthetic, patellar, and antegrade tibial-nail work

positioning.text: Position so the prior midline scar can be reused and extended proximal or distal.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the existing midline TKA scar, the patella, and the tibial tubercle. Note the infrapatellar saphenous branches crossing from medial to lateral.

incision.text: Reuse the longitudinal midline incision and extend it as needed. Raise full-thickness flaps to protect skin blood supply.

superficial_interval.text: Develop full-thickness flaps. Expect minor lateral sensory loss from infrapatellar saphenous branches; significant saphenous-trunk injury is avoidable.

deep_interval.text: Perform a medial parapatellar arthrotomy through the retinaculum and capsule. Extend proximally or toward the tibial tubercle as the fracture requires. Evert the patella only for patellar-component or patellar-fracture work, and avoid avulsing the patellar tendon, especially in flexion.

layers.text: Skin (prior midline), full-thickness flaps, medial retinaculum and capsule, then the joint, distal femur, and proximal tibia.

structures_at_risk.text: The patellar tendon insertion on the tubercle, the extraosseous patellar arterial ring, and infrapatellar saphenous branches are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Patellar eversion in flexion can avulse the patellar tendon from the tubercle.

retraction_hazards.text: Thin flaps jeopardize skin blood supply. Additional quadriceps, lateral-retinacular, or tubercle release may be needed rather than forced eversion.

exposure.text: Gives a universal window for primary or revision TKA and for periprosthetic work needing medial or lateral arthrotomy, patellar fixation, or isolated distal extension for tibial nailing.

limitations.text: Lateral parapatellar arthrotomy is rare. Forced eversion without release risks tendon avulsion.

indications.text: Used whenever the prior midline TKA incision can serve a periprosthetic fracture, patellar fracture, or antegrade tibial nail.

closure.text: Irrigate the joint, close in layers, consider a drain, and close skin with staples or nonabsorbable suture.

complications.text: Complications include patellar-tendon avulsion, skin-flap necrosis, and saphenous neuroma.

procedure_applications.condition: A periprosthetic fracture, patellar fracture, or antegrade tibial nail is handled through the prior midline TKA incision

questions.question: Which arthrotomy is routine through this incision?
When is patellar eversion required?
questions.answer: Only for patellar fractures or revision of the patellar component.

questions.question: What can isolated distal extension be used for?
